title: Economists Compare Countries Using the Price of a Burger
description:
There's a real, semi-serious index that economists use to check if a currency is over or undervalued, and it's based entirely on the price of a Big Mac.

Educational content, not financial advice.

#shorts #financefacts #economics

scenes.text: Since 1986, The Economist magazine has tracked one of the most useful tools in international finance. It's a burger.
It's called the Big Mac Index, and it compares the price of the same burger in different countries.
Because a Big Mac is made almost the same way everywhere, its price reflects local costs, wages, and currency value.
If a Big Mac costs a lot more in one country after converting currencies, that currency might be overvalued.
If it costs a lot less, the currency might be undervalued relative to what it should be.
It's not a precise scientific model, but economists still reference it decades later because it's a surprisingly good rough estimate.
